title: How much does a website cost?
descB: I approach every project through the principle of intentional restraint. Some ideas only require a quiet structure, while others demand a deeper layer of interaction, rhythm, and visual weight to feel complete.
desc: Most projects usually begin around $200 and continue upward depending on the scale, complexity, and overall direction involved. I am still growing into larger productions myself, so while I may not yet feel fully established in handling massive systems, I genuinely enjoy stepping into unfamiliar territory and treating every challenge as part of the process.

title: What kind of services do you offer?
descB: My work exists somewhere between digital architecture and visual storytelling. I enjoy building experiences where movement, typography, spacing, and logic operate together as part of the same atmosphere.
desc: Beyond development, I also explore interface systems, editorial inspired layouts, visual identities, and graphic compositions that rely on balance, structure, and a deliberate sense of control throughout.

title: How long does a project usually take?
descB: I believe meaningful work needs enough room to breathe. Timelines naturally change depending on the complexity of the system, the level of refinement involved, and the amount of friction required to sharpen the result.
desc: Smaller projects may resolve fairly quickly, while larger experiences evolve through multiple stages of iteration. I would rather refine something carefully than ship a version that still feels unresolved.

title: Can you help me redesign my website?
descB: Absolutely. Sometimes a redesign is less about replacing everything entirely and more about removing the unnecessary layers that slowly bury the original clarity of the experience.
desc: I focus on rebuilding rhythm, improving visual hierarchy, and creating interfaces that feel calmer, sharper, and more intentional without losing the identity that made the brand recognizable in the first place.

title: Do you work with clients worldwide?
descB: Distance has never changed the way I think about collaboration. Good communication is usually built through structure, consistency, and mutual clarity rather than physical location alone.
desc: Most workflows already happen remotely, so I keep everything organized through focused updates, intentional feedback cycles, and systems that allow the process to remain steady across different time zones.

title: Can I bring my own design?
descB: Of course. I actually enjoy stepping into existing visual systems and translating them into responsive experiences while preserving the original atmosphere and design language behind them.
desc: During development, I pay close attention to spacing, interaction flow, transitions, and responsiveness so the final implementation still carries the same precision and emotional weight as the source concept.
